description: Use when the user asks whether their CURRENT broadband bill or plan, or a RENEWAL or retention offer their provider quoted, is expensive, competitive or worth switching from. Compares what they pay against comparable deals actually available at their address and returns a computed verdict with true 24-month savings. Present the verdict and figures verbatim rather than deriving your own. Each alternative's cost_24_months is its true cost over the 24-month comparison window; ask get_deal_details for a specific deal's whole-contract total. Set quote_type to 'renewal_offer' when evaluating a renewal quote.

address_label.description: The display_address the user picked from search_addresses, passed back verbatim. Carried into the switch link so the FindBroadband site greets the user with their address instead of asking again.

current_provider.description: The user's current broadband provider, as they said it, e.g. 'Sky' or 'Virgin Media'.

current_speed_mbps.description: The user's current download speed in Mbps. If they only know their package name, ask or estimate from the provider's naming (e.g. 'M125' is about 132).

monthly_bill.description: What the user currently pays per month in GBP (or the renewal price quoted to them).

postcode.description: UK postcode, e.g. 'SS13 1HJ'. When asking, request the postcode and house number or name together in one question rather than two rounds.

quote_type.description: 'renewal_offer' when the user is evaluating a renewal or retention price their provider quoted; 'current_bill' (default) when it is what they pay today.

uprn.description: Property identifier from search_addresses. Pass it whenever the user has picked an address so results become address-precise instead of postcode-wide. Never show this number to the user.

name: check_if_overpaying

gift.description: Provider incentive shown on the deal card: a gift card / reward, or a switching credit. NOT included in any cost figure. A switching credit (e.g. 'up to £300') only offsets early-termination fees the user owes their CURRENT provider (worth £0 to someone out of contract), so explain it as conditional, never as a discount. Gift cards are real value but not bill money.

title: Check if the user is overpaying for broadband
